extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants, and patent office staff (PTAB/Examining Corps)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements, standards, and procedures governing post-grant review (PGR) proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board and related PCT/national-stage procedural provisions relevant to prosecuting international applications into the U.S. national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-grant review provisions of the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (AIA) apply only to patents subject to the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA, except as provided in AIA § 18 and paragraph 2 below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may impose a limit on the number of post-grant reviews that may be instituted under chapter 32 during each of the first four 1-year periods in which these provisions are in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a PGR petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file with the Office a petition to institute a post-grant review of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director shall establish, by regulation, fees to be paid by the person requesting the review, in amounts the Director determines reasonable considering aggregate costs of the post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of challenges in PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in a post-grant review may request to cancel as unpatentable one or more claims of a patent on any ground that could be raised under paragraph (2) or (3) of section 282(b) (relating to invalidity of the patent or any claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a post-grant review may only be filed not later than the date that is 9 months after the date of the grant of the patent or of the issuance of a reissue patent (as the case may be).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of petition (fee and parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition is accompanied by payment of the fee established by the Director and the petition identifies all real parties in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are to be set by the Director under section 321; identification of real parties in interest is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of petition (claims, grounds, evidence particularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition identifies, in writing and with particularity, each claim challenged, the grounds on which the challenge to each claim is based, and the evidence that supports the grounds for the challenge to each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must include copies of patents and printed publications relied upon, and affidavits or declarations if relying on other factual evidence or expert opinions; provide such other information as the Director may require by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition materials to patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner provides copies of any of the documents required under paragraphs (2), (3), and (4) to the patent owner or, if applicable, the designated representative of the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after the receipt of a petition under section 321, the Director shall make the petition available to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bar to PGR by prior civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review may not be instituted if, before the date on which the petition is filed, the petitioner or real party in interest filed a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic stay of civil action after PGR petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner or real party in interest files a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent on or after the date on which the petitioner files a petition for post-grant review, that civil action shall be automatically stayed until either (A) the patent owner moves the court to lift the stay; (B) the patent owner files a civil action or counterclaim alleging infringement; or (C) the petitioner moves the court to dismiss the civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A counterclaim challenging validity does not constitute a civil action for the purpose of this bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunctions timing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a civil action alleging infringement of a patent is filed within 3 months after the date on which the patent is granted, the court may not stay its consideration of the patent owner’s motion for a preliminary injunction on the basis that a petition for post-grant review has been filed or instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder and consolidation of multiple PGR petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one petition for a post-grant review is properly filed against the same patent and the Director determines more than one warrants institution, the Director may consolidate such reviews into a single post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other proceedings; rejection for duplicative arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of any post-grant review, if another proceeding involving the patent is before the Office, the Director may determine the manner in which the post‑grant review or other proceeding may proceed, including stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination; in determining whether to institute, the Director may take into account whether, and reject the petition or request because, the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments previously were presented to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from PGR final written decision — Office proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner (or real party in interest or privy) in a post-grant review that results in a final written decision under section 328(a) may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel from PGR final written decision — civil actions and ITC
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner (or real party in interest or privy) may not assert in a civil action under section 1338 or in an ITC proceeding under section 337 that the claim is invalid on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that post‑grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue patent limitation for PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review may not be instituted if the petition requests cancellation of a claim in a reissue patent that is identical to or narrower than a claim in the original patent from which the reissue patent was issued, and the time limitations in section 321(c) would bar filing a petition for a post-grant review for such original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response right
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post-grant review petition is filed, the patent owner shall have the right to file a preliminary response to the petition, within a time period set by the Director, that sets forth reasons why no post‑grant review should be instituted based upon the failure of the petition to meet any requirement of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution threshold — more likely than not standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize a post-grant review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information presented in the petition, if not rebutted, would demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution alternative basis — novel or unsettled legal question
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution determination may also be satisfied by showing that the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for institution decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall determine whether to institute a post-grant review within 3 months after (1) receiving a preliminary response to the petition, or (2) if no preliminary response is filed, the last date on which such response may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of institution and nonappealability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall notify the petitioner and patent owner, in writing, of the determination whether to institute and make such notice public; the determination by the Director whether to institute a post-grant review shall be final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice shall include the date on which the review shall commence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory prescriptions for PGR conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations providing that the file of any proceeding be made available to the public (with sealing procedures), setting forth standards for showing sufficient grounds to institute review, procedures for submission of supplemental information after the petition is filed, establishing and governing a post-grant review and relationship to other proceedings, standards/procedures for discovery, protective orders, sanctions for abuse, amendment procedures, right to oral hearing, timing of final determination, and opportunity for petitioner comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations must also set standards and procedures for discovery, limit discovery to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party, provide for protective orders, prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery/process, set standards/procedures for allowing the patent owner to move to amend and ensure amendment-supporting information is made public as part of prosecution history, provide right to oral hearing, require final determination within 1 year (with up to 6‑month extension for good cause), and provide at least one opportunity for petitioner to file written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in prescribing PGR regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations, the Director shall consider the effect on the economy, the integrity of the patent system, the efficient administration of the Office, and the ability of the Office to timely complete proceedings instituted under this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limited to directly related evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery in a post-grant review shall be limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders for confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must provide for protective orders governing the exchange and submission of confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for abuse of discovery or process
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or any other improper use of the proceeding, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or an unnecessary increase in the cost of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner motion to amend (one motion standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: During a post-grant review the patent owner may file one motion to amend the patent in one or more of the following ways: (A) cancel any challenged patent claim; (B) for each challenged claim, propose a reasonable number of substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional motions may be permitted upon joint request to materially advance settlement or upon request of the patent owner for good cause shown. An amendment may not enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: In a post-grant review instituted under this chapter, the petitioner shall have the burden of proving a proposition of unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post-grant review is instituted and not dismissed, the PTAB shall issue a final written decision with respect to the patentability of any challenged claim and any new claim added under section 326(d). The Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming claims determined patentable, and incorporating new or amended claims determined patentable after appeals are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following a post-grant review shall have the same effect as specified in section 252 for reissued patents regarding the rights of persons who made, purchased, used, or imported things patented by such claim prior to issuance of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data publication on length of review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make available to the public data describing the length of time between the institution of, and issuance of a final written decision for, each post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and termination of PGR
rubrics_metrics.description: A post-grant review shall be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon the joint request of the petitioner and the patent owner, unless the Office has decided the merits before the request for termination is filed; if terminated as to a petitioner, no estoppel under section 325(e) shall attach to that petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agreement or understanding made in connection with termination must be in writing and a true copy filed in the Office before termination; at request it may be treated as business confidential information and kept separate from the patent file, available only to Federal agencies or to any person on a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT: concept and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for terms used in PCT part: 'treaty' (Patent Cooperation Treaty), 'Regulations' (capitalized = Regulations under the treaty; not capitalized = Office regulations under this title), 'international application', 'international application originating in the United States', 'international application designating the United States', 'Receiving Office', 'International Searching Authority', 'International Preliminary Examining Authority', and 'International Bureau'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms not defined in this part are to be taken in the sense indicated by the treaty and Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office duties and filing language/fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO shall act as a Receiving Office for international applications filed by nationals or residents of the United States and may act for others by agreement; the Office shall perform duties of a Receiving Office, including collection and transmittal of international fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications filed in the PTO shall be filed in English or an English translation shall be filed within a later time fixed by the Director; international/transmittal/search fees shall be paid on filing or within a later time fixed by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTO as International Searching/Preliminary Examining Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTO may act as an International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) with respect to international applications in accordance with agreements with the International Bureau and may discharge duties including collection and transmittal of handling fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling, preliminary examination, and any additional IPEA fees shall be paid within times fixed by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of international application designating the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating the United States shall have the effect, from its international filing date under article 11 of the treaty, of a national application for patent regularly filed in the PTO (with pre-AIA variant noting section 102(e) exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: International stage procedure and excuse for failure to act
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications shall be processed by the PTO when acting as RO/ISA/IPEA in accordance with the treaty, Regulations, and this title; an applicant's failure to act within prescribed time limits may be excused as provided in the treaty and Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority and benefit of prior filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: A national application shall be entitled to the right of priority based on a prior filed international application designating at least one country other than the U.S., and an international application designating the U.S. shall be entitled to priority based on a prior foreign application or prior international application designating another country; entitlement to benefit of prior national/international filing dates follows section 119/120 conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may establish procedures (including fee specified in section 41(a)(7)) to accept unintentionally delayed priority claims or priority claims filed within the additional 2‑month period; if benefit is based on a prior international application that did not originate in the U.S., the Director may require filing a certified copy and translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn international application consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application designating the United States is withdrawn or considered withdrawn before the applicant has complied with applicable section 371(c) requirements, the U.S. designation shall have no effect after the date of withdrawal and be considered not made, unless a claim for benefit was made in a national application or in another application filed before the date of such withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A withdrawn international application may still serve as basis for a priority claim under section 365(a)/(b) or under section 386(a)/(b) if it designated a country other than the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Receiving Office/International Bureau actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Receiving Office other than the PTO has refused to accord an international filing date or held the application withdrawn, the applicant may request review by the Director in compliance with treaty and Regulations; such review may determine the application be considered pending in the national stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review may also be requested where IB deemed the application withdrawn under article 12(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy and foreign filing rules for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed in the PTO shall be subject to chapter 17 (secrecy of certain inventions). Filing an international application in a country other than the U.S. on an invention made in the U.S. shall be considered to constitute filing in a foreign country within the meaning of chapter 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a license to file in a foreign country is refused or an international application is ordered to be kept secret and a permit refused, the PTO acting as RO/ISA/IPEA may not disclose the contents of such application to anyone not authorized to receive such disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage commencement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To commence the national stage, the applicant shall file the national fee (section 41(a)), a copy of the international application (if required), and a translation into English if filed in another language; amendments under article 19 to claims (unless communicated by IB), an oath or declaration complying with section 115, and translations of any annexes to the international preliminary examination report if made in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some requirements may be complied with by the date of commencement or by later time fixed by the Director; failure to comply is regarded as abandonment or cancellation of amendments, and a surcharge may be required to accept late compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing constraints and consequences in national stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The national stage shall commence with expiration of applicable treaty time limits (article 22 or 39), and after national stage commences no patent may be granted or refused before expiration of applicable treaty time limits under article 28 or 41 except with express consent of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may present amendments to specification, claims, and drawings after national stage commencement; national stage may be commenced early at the express request of the applicant if application is in order and subsection (c) requirements have been complied with.
